common_name: October Magic Ivory Camellia (Compact Double White Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; October Magic Ivory keeps a tidy, upright profile that needs little corrective pruning even as a young plant.

directions: October Magic Ivory is a Southern Living Plant Collection introduction valued for fully double, creamy-white, carnation-like blooms with ruffled petals that open over a long fall-into-winter season on a compact, upright plant reaching roughly 6-8 feet tall. Its restrained size and vertical branching habit make it a good fit for foundation plantings, narrow side yards, and large patio containers where a spreading sasanqua would quickly outgrow the space. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in part shade, since the pale flower color can bleach or brown faster in hot, unfiltered afternoon sun. Feed with an acid-forming camellia fertilizer in early spring and again after the fall bloom flush, and mulch generously to buffer soil moisture and temperature.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Autumn Rocket's narrow, columnar habit suits tight side yards and vertical accents better than most sasanquas.

directions: Autumn Rocket was bred by Dr. James Habel of Suffolk, Virginia for an unusually narrow, columnar growth habit, reaching 8-10 feet tall but only 3-4 feet wide, which makes it one of the few sasanquas useful for tight side yards, narrow screens, or a strong vertical accent without heavy shearing. Deceptively pink buds open in fall to double, pure-white flowers with a bright center of yellow stamens against dark, glossy foliage. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with part-shade to full-sun exposure, and site out of drying winter wind, which can desiccate the tall, narrow canopy faster than a broader shrub form. Prune lightly right after bloom only to maintain the columnar line, since the plant's natural habit already does most of the shaping work.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in dappled shade; Cotton Candy is among the earliest sasanquas to color up, often opening before hard fall frosts arrive.

directions: Cotton Candy produces large, ruffled, semi-double flowers in a clear cotton-candy pink with a yellow-stamened eye, fading toward white as each bloom ages, giving a two-tone effect across the shrub during its early-to-mid fall bloom window. The upright habit and small, glossy, pointed dark-green leaves reach roughly 6-8 feet tall and 4-6 feet wide at maturity, making it a manageable specimen or informal hedge plant. Grow in loose, organically rich, acidic soil with dependable moisture while flower buds are forming in late summer, and provide sun-dappled shade rather than deep shade, which slows bloom production. Once established the shrub tolerates brief dry spells, but even watering during the bud-set period improves flower size and count.

common_name: Silver Dollar Camellia (Compact Double White Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.1-6.0), humus-rich soil in filtered shade; Silver Dollar's dense, mounding form fills out well without heavy pruning.

directions: Introduced by Nuccio's Nurseries of Altadena, California in 1985, Silver Dollar bears small, double, informally arranged flowers in silvery white, sometimes lightly splashed with pink on the reverse of the petals, centered by golden stamens. The dense, mounding habit and comparatively small, dark-green leaves give the shrub a fine-textured look distinct from larger-leaved sasanqua selections, and mature plants can reach 6-12 feet tall and equally wide if left unpruned. Grow in acidic, well-drained soil with moderate, consistent moisture and filtered shade, since sasanquas generally tolerate more sun than japonica camellias but Silver Dollar's pale flowers hold their color longer out of harsh afternoon exposure. Shape lightly right after the fall-to-winter bloom period to control the eventual spread if a tighter form is wanted.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Sparkling Burgundy responds well to espalier or hedge training against a wall or fence.

directions: Sparkling Burgundy carries showy, peony-form flowers in a deep ruby-red with a subtle lavender undertone, scattered with gold stamens, opening over a long early-season window from October into January in mild climates. The moderate-growing shrub matures to roughly 6-10 feet tall and 4-8 feet wide with glossy, elliptical, dark-green foliage, versatile enough for a flowering hedge, screen, espalier, or accent planting near a patio where the rich flower color reads best up close. Plant in acidic, well-drained soil enriched with organic matter, and give it partial shade with protection from harsh midday sun, which can fade the deep burgundy tone faster than filtered light. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and again after bloom, and prune promptly once flowering ends to preserve next year's bud set.

common_name: Buttermint Camellia (Cream and Butter-Yellow Winter-Blooming Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.1-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial sun; Buttermint's sasanqua-oleifera parentage gives it better cold tolerance than most fall-blooming camellias.

directions: Buttermint is a sasanqua-oleifera hybrid selected for small, button-like, formal double flowers in creamy white with butter-yellow centers and a mild, sweet fragrance, opening later than most sasanquas from late winter into early spring on a compact plant about 6 feet tall and 4-5 feet wide. Its oleifera parentage lends noticeably improved cold hardiness compared with straight sasanqua cultivars, allowing gardeners in USDA zone 6b to grow a camellia that would otherwise need zone 7 or warmer protection. Grow in acidic, well-drained, organically rich soil in partial sun, giving it more light than a japonica camellia would tolerate but with some afternoon shelter in hot-summer climates. Fertilize with an acid-forming camellia formula in early spring after bloom finishes, and mulch well to protect roots through winter cold snaps.
